issues_detected.description: No top-level `doi` slot is populated even though the record's own `citation` names a dataset DOI ('https://doi.org/10.18130/V3/HIGT4C') and `version_access.latest_version_doi` gives 'doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; the DOI is only carried on the four `resources` entries
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate top-level `doi` with the latest release DOI (10.18130/V3/HIGT4C) so persistent-identifier checks resolve at the dataset level

issues_detected.description: Release version numbers are non-monotonic across releases: the June 2025 and October 2025 releases are 'version: 2.1' while the newer June 2026 release is 'version: 2.0'. The record explains this ('Release version numbers are recorded as the release page states them (1.4, 2.1, 2.1, 2.0)') but a reader of `version_access.versions_available` sees the latest release carrying a lower number than its predecessors
issues_detected.recommendation: Add a sentence to `version_details` stating that version numbers are per-deposit Dataverse counters, not a programme-wide sequence

issues_detected.description: Project end dates disagree across fields: `updates.update_details` and `collection_timeframes` state 'through the end of the project in November 2026' while the funders entry states 'project start 2022-09-01 and project end 2026-08-31'. The record flags this in `source_caveats` item (4) and attributes each to its tier, so it is disclosed rather than hidden
issues_detected.recommendation: None required for the record; downstream users should treat the sustainability horizon as 2026-08-31 to 2026-11 pending clarification

issues_detected.description: The `data_topic` for AP-MS uses a non-OBO-PURL form 'http://www.bioassayontology.org/bao#BAO_0002603' whereas the other instances use OBO PURLs ('http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_0008104', 'http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/NCIT_C18469'); inconsistent IRI style reduces interoperability of the ontology annotations
The generation header states '# Generated: 2026-08-26' while the run label is '2026-08-24_claude-opus-5-claudecode-generic-v5_rep2'; the record's own provenance date postdates its label by two days
issues_detected.recommendation: Confirm the label/generation date relationship in the run provenance record

issues_detected.description: Distribution formats are ZIP, JSON and HTML only; the scientific content formats inside the ZIP archives (image formats, mass spectrometry tables, sequence formats) are never named, so `distribution_formats` describes the packaging rather than the data. The record states 'Data files are distributed as ZIP archives' and the June 2026 files 'carry name, path, checksum and format only'
issues_detected.recommendation: Where sources permit, name the inner file formats (e.g. image and table formats) per archive

issues_detected.description: External repository links carry no accession identifiers: 'The captured release pages give the link text but no MassIVE accession identifiers', 'no BioProject accession identifier', 'no Figshare accession identifier'. The external resources are therefore named but not resolvable from the record
issues_detected.recommendation: Add MassIVE, BioProject and Figshare accessions once available so the cross-repository links are actionable

issues_detected.description: Use-guidance coverage is partial: `intended_uses` (4) and `prohibited_uses` (2) are populated but there are no `discouraged_uses` and no `future_use_impacts`; the known_limitations statement that 'the current release is most suitable for bioinformatics analysis of the individual datasets rather than for joint multimodal analysis' is a natural discouraged use that is not expressed in the use-guidance slots
issues_detected.recommendation: Add a `discouraged_uses` entry for joint multimodal analysis and a `future_use_impacts` entry covering dual-use and commercialisation supervision already described under `data_governance.access_review_process`

semantic_insights: Human-subjects logic is internally consistent: `human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects: false`, 'Human Subjects: No, De-identified Samples: Yes, and FDA Regulated: No', and `ethical_reviews` explicitly states 'No institutional review board approval is claimed by any source in the bundle' rather than fabricating an IRB

Deidentification claim is appropriate for the data type: 'commercially available de-identified human cell lines' that 'cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject', with the honest caveat 'No source in the bundle names a de-identification method or a list of identifiers removed, so neither is asserted'
All NIH grant numbers follow NIH format: '1OT2OD032742-01', '3OT2OD032742-01S2', '5U54HG012513-02'; core project OT2OD032742 is correctly tied to principal investigator 'IDEKER, TREY'

DOI prefixes are registrar-plausible: 10.18130 (University of Virginia LibraData Dataverse) for the four release DOIs and DXWOS5; 10.1101 (bioRxiv) for the two preprints; 10.1038 for the Nature paper the record deliberately excludes
Cell-line RRIDs are correctly formatted: 'MDA-MB-468 (RRID:CVCL_0419)' and 'KOLF2.1J (RRID:CVCL_B5P3)'

Temporal ordering is consistent: releases published 2025-03-03, 2025-07-01, 2025-10-31, 2026-06-17 with later staged file dates (2025-10-22, 2025-12-22, 2026-07-15) documented per release; the record correctly refuses to use the repository 'Data Creation Date' of 2025-02-27 as a collection date

Scope discipline: the Nature 2025 U2OS cell-map paper is identified as 'a distinct dataset' and 'not merged into this record', and the DXWOS5 release is recorded as an earlier version rather than a resource

FAIR alignment: license CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 matches `data_use_permission: no_commercial_use` and the prohibited commercial-use entry; every file is 'File Access: Public' consistent with `confidentiality_level: unrestricted`
Bias taxonomy is used: `bias_type: representation_bias` with `affected_subsets` naming both cell-line data families

Source conflicts (release date, protein counts 523/464/563, institutions, governance body name, Sali affiliation, perturb-seq gene counts) are resolved by an explicit tier ranking and each resolution is recorded

strengths: Exhaustive, checksummed file enumeration across four DOI-identified releases with per-file sizes and publication dates
Complete funding record with three NIH award numbers in valid format, award amount and PI, plus affiliations for all 48 creators

Governance and access documentation is complete and consistent: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, IP holders, FDA status, unrestricted confidentiality, governance contact, and a fully described download route including the Data Access API
Version history and sustainability are documented end to end, with six versions, errata, quarterly update plan and institutional preservation commitment
Source conflicts are resolved by an explicit tier ranking and every unasserted value is accompanied by a stated reason
weaknesses: Only container formats (ZIP/JSON/HTML) are named; the scientific data formats inside archives are not
External repository links (MassIVE, BioProject, Figshare) have no accession identifiers
Use guidance lacks `discouraged_uses` and `future_use_impacts`; bias documentation has one entry and no fairness analysis
Software transparency limited to FAIRSCAPE without a version; QC criteria for released data unknown
recommendations: Populate top-level `doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C` and add `variables` for the principal data tables where sources permit
Name inner file formats per archive (image, mass spectrometry and sequence formats)
Add MassIVE, BioProject and Figshare accessions to `external_resources` when they appear in source pages
Add `discouraged_uses` (joint multimodal analysis given incomplete modality overlap) and `future_use_impacts` (commercialisation and dual-licensing supervision)
Add a `selection_bias` entry reflecting the targeted 100 chromatin modifier / 100 metabolic enzyme panel, and record FAIRSCAPE and MuSIC pipeline versions
